name: Tsodilo
description: Rising abruptly from the flat Kalahari Desert in northwestern Botswana, the Tsodilo Hills are three main rock outcrops known as the Male, Female and Child hills. Over 4,500 paintings are packed into just 10 square kilometres, earning the site the nickname "Louvre of the Desert." People have lived here for at least 100,000 years, and local communities still regard the hills as a home of ancestral spirits.
